fixes.title: Files & Storage says 'Last backup: Never' while Settings > Advanced > Backup & Restore says 'Last Full Backup: Aug 2, 2026 10:30' - same app, same second, same fact
fixes.summary: AutoSaveSettings (the Auto-Save & Backups half of the merged Files & Storage page) watched the raw autoSaveServiceProvider and mirrored that instance's statusStream into local state. That provider ref.watches backendProvider, so it is rebuilt on every backend swap and hands back an un-started service whose _status.lastBackup is null - hence 'Never' / 'Pending' with autosave.last_backup_at persisted and .nsbackup files on disk. The page now depends on autoSaveLifecycleProvider (the only provider that reads the persisted keys and calls start(config, lastBackup)) and renders autoSaveStatusProvider - the same DB-backed source Backup & Restore reads - falling back to the hydrated service's own status while the stream's first event is in flight. The manual StreamSubscription/_currentStatus mirror is gone. Watching the lifecycle provider means opening this page now genuinely starts the host scheduler if the entry point had not, which is the honest behaviour: a page showing 'every 24h' while nothing is scheduled would be the same class of lie.
fixes.test: 'Status shows the persisted last backup, not "Never"' in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/auto_save_service.dart:690 - autoSaveServiceProvider ref.watches backendProvider, so a backend swap silently replaces the running scheduler with a fresh un-started one and start() begins with `if (_started) return;`, meaning a service started without arguments can never be hydrated afterwards. The UI now routes around this, but the provider itself should either not depend on backendProvider or should re-run the lifecycle hydration on rebuild.
fixes.caveats: Verified by restoring auto_save_settings.dart to HEAD: the test fails with 'Found 0 widgets with text "2h ago"' (the card renders 'Never'), then passes again with the fix. auto_save_settings.dart is not literally in my ownership list but it is the other half of the Files & Storage unit named by these findings and appears in no other agent's findings file. Because the page now starts a real scheduler, two pre-existing tests that render this pane began tripping flutter_test's pending-timer invariant (settings_screen_test.dart merged-key tests, settings_section_index_test.dart every-key loop); both now stop the scheduler inside the test body. Neither test file is claimed by another agent's findings.

fixes.title: INDI 'Test Connection' reports a green 'Connected. Found 0 devices.' for an address nothing can connect to
fixes.summary: Confirmed real and diagnosed, but every line that has to change is outside my files. The Rust side is honest (native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/discovery.rs maps the failure to SkotiqError::connection_failed) and the dialog already has a catch branch that would render 'Connection failed: $e'. The swallow is in skotiq_core: FfiBackend._discoverAddressDevices (packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart:86-101) catches every exception, logs a warning and returns const <DeviceInfo>[], which makes indi_server_dialog.dart's catch unreachable and its success string unconditional. The swallow exists for the startup sweep (unified_discovery_provider.dart:380), which must not fail closed - so the fix is to move it, not delete it.
fixes.needs_shared_change: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/ffi_backend/discovery_camera_operations.dart: delete the try/catch in _discoverAddressDevices (86-101) so discoverIndiAtAddress and discoverAlpacaAtAddress propagate the bridge error, matching DisconnectedBackend (which throws not-connected) and NetworkBackend (which propagates). Move the 'warn and return no devices' swallow to its one background caller, packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/unified_discovery_provider.dart:~380, where an unreachable configured address must not abort the whole startup sweep. THEN in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/equipment/dialogs/indi_server_dialog.dart:126-131, distinguish the two outcomes the probe can now report: an empty list is 'Connected, but the server reports no drivers.' and the catch branch (already written, currently unreachable) says 'No INDI server answered at <host>:<port>: $e'. NOTE: indi_server_dialog.dart is owned by the equipment/diagnostics/shell agent, whose findings file carries this same defect as unit screen:equipment/indi_server_dialog.dart - the two halves should land together, and the core half is the one that actually unblocks it.
fixes.test: None written - a test asserting the dialog reports a failure would pass only after the core change, so it belongs with that change. The reachable assertion once the core swallow moves: pump IndiServerDialog with a deviceServiceProvider whose discoverIndiAtAddress throws, tap Test Connection, expect find.textContaining('Connection failed') and find.textContaining('Connected.') findsNothing.
fixes.caveats: Not fixed because the cause is a shared skotiq_core file and the only UI file involved belongs to a concurrently-running agent that has the identical finding assigned. Cause verified by reading the code, not by re-running the app.

fixes.title: Auto-Save & Backups renders compiled-in defaults instead of the saved settings, and changing any one field silently overwrites the other four
fixes.summary: Same root cause as the 'Never' card, with a data-loss tail: the page rendered service.config from the un-hydrated raw service (defaults: sequence auto-save off, 7 backups, 2 min) and _updateConfig did service.config.copyWith(...) on that same stale object, which _persistAutoSaveConfig then wrote back across ALL FIVE autosave.* keys. The page now renders and edits the config from autoSaveLifecycleProvider's hydrated service, so the copyWith baseline is what is on disk. The three numeric fields also pass the hydrated value as SettingsNumberInput.authoritativeValue (+ authorityKey: service) instead of being pre-seeded from initState - that is the design system's own 'the provider owns this number' mechanism, and it re-seeds correctly when the service instance changes while preserving an in-progress edit.
fixes.test: 'renders the persisted schedule rather than compiled-in defaults' and 'editing one field does not overwrite the other saved settings' in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/auto_save_settings_hydration_test.dart
fixes.caveats: Both tests fail against HEAD (the switch reads false where true was persisted; the config handed to the persistence seam carries sequenceEnabled=false / maxBackups=7 instead of true / 50) and pass with the fix. I deliberately did NOT make the persist step write only the changed keys as the finding proposed: _persistAutoSaveConfig lives in skotiq_core, and more importantly a partial write would have relocated the defect rather than fixed it - the in-memory config object was the wrong thing, so a partial write would have left the running scheduler on a schedule the database disagrees with. Fixing the baseline fixes both halves. The pre-existing auto_save_settings_failure_test.dart still passes.

fixes.title: One failed 'Connect to Server' attempt drops the app out of Local mode permanently - every screen gets an undismissable red 'Error: not connected to server' banner and there is no way back without a restart
fixes.summary: Two changes in connection_settings.dart. (1) The connect dialog now records the backend it is about to displace; if that was a local FfiBackend (neither NetworkBackend nor DisconnectedBackend) and the handshake fails, it calls backendProvider.notifier.useLocalBackend() to put local mode back, and says so ('Still working locally on this computer.') alongside the real failure - or reports honestly if the restore itself failed. Reaching an OPTIONAL remote host can no longer cost the machine that owns the hardware its local session, and with a local backend installed the shell's DisconnectedBackend-keyed red banner never appears. (2) A 'Work Locally' row now appears on the Connection page whenever the app is sitting on a DisconnectedBackend on a desktop platform - useLocalBackend() previously had NO caller anywhere in the UI, which is exactly why relaunching was the only way out. The row is gated to Linux/macOS/Windows because only the desktop/headless entry points install a local backend; on a phone it would be a button to nowhere.
fixes.needs_shared_change: OPTIONAL follow-up, not required by the tests above: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/backend_provider.dart:194-228 _rollbackFailedConnect still installs a fresh DisconnectedBackend on a failed connect rather than restoring the backend it displaced. Fixing it there would cover the other connect call sites (apps/mobile reconnect ops, pairing, headless auto-connect) in one place; my change covers the Settings > Connection path only. Separately, packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/shell/app_shell.dart:653-671 (shell agent's file) could carry a 'Work locally' action on the banner itself, as the finding suggested.
fixes.test: 'a failed connect leaves the machine in local mode' and 'a disconnected desktop is offered a way back to local mode' in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/settings/connection_settings_local_fallback_test.dart
fixes.caveats: Verified by restoring connection_settings.dart to HEAD: test 1 fails (useLocalBackend called 0 times, the backend stays a DisconnectedBackend) and test 2 fails (no 'Work Locally' button exists); both pass with the fix. The test notifier reproduces the production failure path (install DisconnectedBackend, then throw) rather than opening a socket. The pre-existing connection_settings_connection_truth_test.dart and platform_capabilities_settings_test.dart still pass. Not validated live against a running desktop instance.
